expectations.text: States plainly that the recent-charge lookup is not sufficient
expectations.evidence: "Short answer: no, that guard is not enough. It changes the shape of the bug, it doesn't close the hazard"

expectations.text: Identifies the lookup as a check-then-act race rather than a device
expectations.evidence: "TOCTOU race. Redelivery under a timeout is exactly the condition that produces two workers (or two rapid attempts) racing: both read 'no recent matching charge,' both proceed, both charge. The check and the charge aren't atomic"

expectations.text: Recommends a required idempotency key on the charge path
expectations.evidence: "pass a stable Idempotency-Key (order/invoice ID, not a timestamp) on every Stripe charge call"

expectations.text: Recommends a database unique constraint backing the idempotency key
expectations.evidence: "unique DB constraint on (order_id) or (idempotency_key) in your own charges table"

expectations.text: Separates the defect from the mistake from the underlying system hazard
expectations.evidence: Explicitly lists: Defect (340 charged twice), Mistake (redelivery), Hazard (no enforced idempotency)

expectations.text: Locates the hazard as a system property rather than as a worker bug or human error
expectations.evidence: "the charge path has no enforced idempotency — nothing (API contract, DB constraint, or type) makes it impossible"

expectations.text: Sweeps for other non-idempotent side effects reachable from a retry
expectations.evidence: "Class sweep (do before closing this out): any other consumer on that same at-least-once queue with a non-idempotent side effect — refund issuance, customer emails/webhooks, ledger postings, inventory decrements"

expectations.text: Treats 'second time this happened' as evidence for pushing to a Control-rung device
expectations.evidence: "Why this is the second time: if the first incident's fix was also a check/detection-style patch rather than a structural constraint, that's the pattern — fixes are landing at the mistake level... The hazard survives and resurfaces"

expectations.text: Attributes cause to the system, not to any person
expectations.evidence: "the charge path has no enforced idempotency" — system design issue, not worker or human failure
